title: Hoist over-travel and slack-rope protection
nl_spec: A hoist is jogged up and down by momentary RaiseCmd and LowerCmd. Two over-travel limit switches and a slack-rope switch are wired normally-closed (TRUE = healthy/clear, FALSE = tripped): UpperLimitOK = FALSE means the upper over-travel limit is reached, LowerLimitOK = FALSE means the lower over-travel limit is reached, SlackRopeOK = FALSE means slack rope is detected. Raising is inhibited when the upper limit is reached; lowering is inhibited when the lower limit is reached OR when slack rope is detected (to prevent piling rope). Up and down must never be commanded together, and a simultaneous raise+lower request produces no motion. EStop is the emergency stop, normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated); when activated all motion stops. A holding brake output BrakeSet must be engaged (TRUE) whenever the hoist is not moving. (Note: the physical brake coil is the inverse of the logical BrakeSet state - real hoist brakes are spring-applied and power-released, so BrakeSet = TRUE, brake engaged, corresponds to the brake coil being de-energized.) Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named hoist with inputs RaiseCmd, LowerCmd, UpperLimitOK, LowerLimitOK, SlackRopeOK, EStop and outputs HoistUp, HoistDown, BrakeSet.

interface.name: UpperLimitOK
interface.description: Upper over-travel limit, normally-closed: TRUE = clear, FALSE = limit reached

interface.name: LowerLimitOK
interface.description: Lower over-travel limit, normally-closed: TRUE = clear, FALSE = limit reached

interface.name: SlackRopeOK
interface.description: Slack-rope switch, normally-closed: TRUE = rope taut, FALSE = slack detected

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: On emergency stop (EStop = FALSE), there is no motion.
When the upper over-travel limit is reached, raising is inhibited.
When slack rope is detected, lowering is inhibited.
Up and down are never commanded at the same time.
Positive obligation: whenever the hoist is not moving, the holding brake is engaged.
When the lower over-travel limit is reached, lowering is inhibited.
A simultaneous raise+lower request produces no motion.

scenarios.description: Normal raise, then lower, with brake tracking motion
Upper over-travel blocks raise; slack rope blocks lower
Emergency stop stops motion and sets the brake

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: directional motion protection - the upper limit inhibits ONLY raising and the lower limit / slack rope inhibit ONLY lowering (asymmetric), plus a positive brake-engagement obligation. Distinct from generic multi-guard interlocks (guards are direction-specific, not a single permissive AND) and from two-hand control. The up/down mutual-exclusion appears only as a secondary property, not the primary structure.
